INVENTORY QUESTIONS

Dead stock, forecasting, and staying in sync online.

What does Jwero do for a jewellery inventory manager?

Jwero tracks every tagged jewellery piece on its own, with its location and full movement history. You print barcode tags, run scheduled scan counts with a discrepancy list, record adjustments with reasons, move stock between branches, track pieces on memo, trial or consignment, open and close safes with a count, and see stock value and ageing reports.

Can Jwero tell me my dead stock?

Yes, ageing bands (0–30, 31–90, 91–180, 180+ days) and fast/slow-mover views show exactly which pieces are sitting, for how long, and what they’re worth at today’s rate.

Does it forecast demand or tell me what to order?

Not yet, predictive demand forecasting is on the roadmap, not shipped. What Jwero gives you today is visibility: ageing, valuation and mover data you use to make the reorder call yourself, not a prediction it makes for you.

Does this replace our physical stocktake?

No, but it makes it faster and less of a surprise-finding exercise, ageing and valuation are visible continuously, so a stocktake confirms what you already suspected rather than revealing it cold.

Does inventory stay in sync if we also sell on Shopify or Unicommerce?

Yes, Shopify, WooCommerce and Unicommerce connectors sync stock and orders both ways, so a piece sold online doesn’t sit as available in your in-store count.

Does Jwero count raw gold and reconcile it?

Not yet. Jwero shows book balances of metal by party and lot, but a physical metal count and reconciliation screen is not available. Finished pieces are counted by scan; raw metal counts are done outside Jwero for now.

Can I stop people adjusting stock without a reason?

Stock adjustments are recorded with reasons and every movement is logged with who did it. Sensitive actions can be held in approval queues until a manager approves them.

How do I get my existing stock in?

Import from a CSV or Excel sheet, map the columns to jewellery fields like metal, purity, weights and stones, and Jwero creates the products. Tags are then printed from templates.
